facts.statement: The genus Aegialornis was described by Richard Lydekker in 1891.
Fossils of Aegialornis date from the Early to Late Eocene epoch.
Aegialornis is classified as a genus of prehistoric apodiform birds.
facts.quote: Aegialornis is a genus of prehistoric apodiform birds.

facts.statement: Aegialornis formed a distinct family known as the Aegialornithidae.
facts.quote: It formed a distinct family, the Aegialornithidae

facts.statement: Aegialornis is not considered a direct ancestor of modern swifts but represents a group that retained basal morphology.
facts.quote: They do not appear to be a direct ancestor of modern swifts, however, but rather a group that retained an overall basal morphology.

facts.statement: Aegialornis birds were physically similar to modern treeswifts.
facts.quote: Altogether, they were not too dissimilar from modern treeswifts.

facts.statement: Aegialornis possessed sickle-shaped wings similar to those of modern swifts.
facts.quote: but already having sickle-shaped wings like them

facts.statement: Fossils of Aegialornis have been found in Middle to Late Eocene deposits in Germany and France.
facts.quote: Fossils of Aegialornis have been found in Middle to Late Eocene deposits of Germany and France.

facts.statement: It is debated whether an Early Eocene record from the Nanjemoy Formation in Virginia belongs to Aegialornis, as apodiform birds may not have existed there until after the Eocene.
facts.quote: An Early Eocene record from the Nanjemoy Formation of Virginia, United States (USNM 496384) is very doubtful, as apodiform birds seem not to have occurred there until after the Eocene.

facts.statement: The taxonomy of Aegialornis species is debated, with some researchers considering A. germanicus and A. leenhardti as junior synonyms of A. gallicus.
facts.quote: The taxonomy of the species is quite convoluted, with both the smaller A. germanicus and the larger A. leenhardti being sometimes considered junior synonyms of A. gallicus

facts.statement: It is debated whether A. broweri is based on small individuals of A. wetmorei, and the proposal to separate them into the genus Mesogiornis has not found general acceptance.
facts.quote: Similarly, A. broweri is occasionally considered to be based on small individuals of A. wetmorei, and these latter two taxa were recently separated as genus Mesogiornis (Mlíkovský, 2002); this does not appear to have found general acceptance however.

facts.statement: It is uncertain which other genera should be included in the family Aegialornithidae.
facts.quote: Which genera apart from the present one should be included in the Aegialornithidae is not quite certain.

facts.statement: The classification of Cypselavus is debated, with it being considered either an aegialornithid or a treeswift.
facts.quote: Cypselavus is either an aegialornithid or a treeswift.

facts.statement: The inclusion of the Jungornithidae family in the Aegialornithidae is controversial.
facts.quote: The latter group is sometimes controversially included in the Aegialornithidae, as are the Jungornithidae, another prehistoric apodiform family

facts.statement: The time range for Aegialornis is estimated between 41.03 and 37.71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bartonian to Bartonian (41.03 to 37.71 million years ago)
